3/16 10:15 AM Update: The Gondola is on wind hold.
Good morning skiers and riders! What a week it has been...thanks for your patience as things unfolded and we got terrain open. Highway 410 is open we are now back to normal operations. Coverage is the best it's been all season! Last night we received some additional precipitation of the liquid variety and with warmer temps today, off-piste conditions may be quite variable. Groomers are expected to be ripping today, with spring slush on deck for the afternoon. We have chances of light precip and moderate winds towards the afternoon. Right now, we have partly cloudy skies.
Terrain Parks: Sudden Drop and Arwine's Jump Line are open. 

Be aware of deep snow hazards today: Ski and ride with a partner, keep them in sight, and have a plan to check in. Always ski and ride in control. Read up on Tree Well Safety here. Obey all closures and do not duck ropes.

Events:
  • Treasure Hunt Tuesday + St Patty's Day Golden Keg Hunt is on tomorrow! Look on social stories for hints to find the goods around the mountain. 
  • $62 Tuesday is on tomorrow, and every Tuesday for the rest of season! In honor of our founding year 1962, score day tickets for just $62!
  • Toyota Free Ski Thursday is just a couple days away! Drive your Toyota, Scion, or Lexus vehicle to Crystal Mountain on March 19, and grab one free lift ticket for the day. See Full details here.

Mountain Weather 3/15/2026 4:20pm 

Forecaster: Morgan McGonagle
  
Synopsis: Well folks, that was a wild one. I hope you got some soft cold turns today, because things are taking a quick turn from cool and dry to warm and wet starting this evening. As a sharp warm front lifts over the region, milder air will make its way towards us from the SW, pushing snow levels up to 8000’. With the southwesterly nature of this front, we could get a decent block from Tahoma, keeping our moisture totals around a quarter inch of water. Freezing levels will continue to rise on Monday, and liquid will continue to fall lightly from the sky until early afternoon.
 Sunday Night:
Sky Cover: Cloudy with light precip
Freezing Elevation: 5500' increasing to 8000'
12hr Precip: 0.25” WE with a Trace to 2" snow above 5500'
Wind Trends: Moderate WSW
Monday:
Sky Cover: Cloudy with rain
Freezing Elevation: 10,000’
12hr Precip: LT 0.25” WE 
Wind Trends: Moderate WSW with Strong gusts at ridgetops
Monday Night:
Sky Cover: Mostly cloudy 
Freezing Elevation: 10,000’
12hr Precip: Little to none 
Wind Trends: Moderate WSW with Strong gusts at ridgetops
Extended:   
Unfortunately, the hose of warm moisture is only going to widen its girth on Tuesday starting midday and it doesn’t appear to let up until the weekend. Grab your rubbers and your umbrella if you’re heading up to ski this week.

*Daily Summaries: 12hr period representing 4am-4pm or 4pm-4am data
*Freezing Elevation (ft): Approximate elevation above sea level where the air temperature reaches 32 degree F
